sense.text:
We’re living in very dangerous, perilous times: chemical outbreaks popping up one after another, the train derailment in East Palestine, Ohio, the water contaminated, and the relief refused. It’s not by coincidence. There are factors out there and things we cannot control, things we cannot see, so we want to make sure we’re getting ourselves aligned.

“Mine enemies would daily swallow me up: for they be many that fight against me, O thou most High.” We have many enemies, including the number one enemy, Esau.

“What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee. In God I will praise his word, in God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.” We got to be in that mindset. Even though we see the dangerous things coming, and it’s coming from the governments and from all different angles, we still got to trust in the Most High, brothers and sisters.
“Every day they wrest my words: all their thoughts are against me for evil.” Read it together with 1 Maccabees 3:52: the enemy’s thoughts are against us for evil every day.

precepts.why:
“And lo, the heathen are assembled together against us to destroy us”. The scriptures are telling us we have opposition, opposition on every side, brothers and sisters.

“What things they imagine against us, thou knowest.” The things they imagine against us, only God knows the insides and outs. This is a chemical disaster, and the EPA did not deem it necessary, FEMA did not deem it necessary, and the Biden administration did not deem it necessary to provide relief. When you see atrocities and perils and situations like this take place, understand, it’s against the children of Israel.

Only God knows, so that’s what we got to do: put our trust in the Lord. We can’t be panicking out here going crazy. Now’s the time to increase in righteousness.

“And thou, that hast been the author of all mischief against the Hebrews”. The author of all mischief against who? Against the Hebrews. Do not think for one second, brothers and sisters, that this ain’t got nothing to do with us. Do not be simple and think that this is an attack on all humanity. It’s never been like that. Since day one, it’s always been against us.

“Shalt not escape the hands of God”: the Most High is not going to allow them to fulfill their full enterprise. At the end of the day, they wish they could slaughter us all, and they have different techniques: the foods we eat, and disasters like this. They have the technology to target a specific demographic.

As you see the iniquity abounding, the righteousness got to abound. How else are we going to be able to combat all the wickedness that’s surrounding us on the day-to-day?

“But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” So, knowing what’s in front of us, knowing what we’re facing and what we’re up against, we got to crank it up, turn up and increase in righteousness. That is tapping into our full potential.

sense.text:
“So I considered the world, and, behold, there was peril because of the devices that were come into it.” The devices it’s talking about are sin, wickedness. Remember, when we were with the Most High, we agreed to do his will, but when we got here, what took place? Evil, iniquity, sin. And because of that, peril was created.

Peril is exposure to the risk of being injured, destroyed, or lost. Danger, danger, danger. Think about the toxic chemicals out there: they’re saying it could cause liver damage, which is going to lead to other issues, other risk of injury.

“And I saw, and spared it greatly”: there is a God. God saw the evils, God saw a lot of danger, the perils, and he spared it greatly.

“And have kept me a grape of the cluster”. That’s you, righteous Israelites, who are going to increase in these last days. They passed homosexual marriage, men can have periods now, men can now give birth; all of this wickedness is going around, but God said he kept him a grape of the cluster. Not the whole cluster, but he kept him some of the righteous of the cluster, “and a plant of a great people.”

So there’s always hope, and that’s why we got to keep the faith and stay in the secret place of the Most High, and that’s this Bible. When we see all of these evils increasing, we got to increase in our studies, and most importantly, we got to tap into the full potential that God created us to be.

Some exhortation. The brethren at Jerusalem “wish unto the brethren, the Jews that are throughout Egypt health and peace”. That’s what we got to do: wish and pray for our brothers and sisters in our various captivities, scattered abroad. We got to pray for health and peace for one another.

“God be gracious unto you, and remember his covenant that he made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, his faithful servants”. That’s the key. Verse 1 says health and peace, and verse 2 shows the only way we’re going to get that health and peace: if we remember his covenant.

“And give you all an heart to serve him, and to do his will, with a good courage”. Courage is the opposite of fear. When you read Wisdom of Solomon 8, it describes the attributes that come along with wisdom, and fortitude is one of them: the ability to see what’s going on, the perils, and still keep your composure and deal with it as it comes. “With a good courage and a willing mind”.

“And open your hearts in his law and commandments, and send you peace, And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.” Our fortitude and our courage come from our trust in God. That’s it. So let’s focus on that and build on it: build on our faith, and on our focus and belief that God will deliver us from these perils.

precepts.why: Good health, because of “the pestilence that walketh in darkness”. You got these different diseases, and now something new with these toxic chemical outbreaks. You can’t see all of that. It already burned; it’s already in the air. You’re going to work every day, or school, or the grocery store, and that pestilence is moving around in darkness, something you cannot see. That’s why we got to pray for one another, and pray for health for our brothers and sisters.

Verse 1 says health and peace, and verse 2 says the only way we get it is if we remember his covenant. “And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.”

When all else fails and everything’s hit the fan, where there’s distress of nations, where there’s chaos, we are going to be stable. We’re going to be at peace. Why? Because we are applying the covenant, and we’re applying that wisdom and knowledge. The fear of the Lord is his treasure.

Because it says peace. “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. God will keep him in perfect peace if his mind is stayed on him. So throughout the turmoil, throughout the chaos, we got to keep our minds focused on doing the work of the Lord: studying, exhorting one another.

Don’t be the brother or sister who’s bringing problems and opposition. Be the brother or sister who’s trying to work together with the body, who’s trying to exhort one another. Be that person in these last days.

“Insomuch as God hath delivered us from great perils, we thank him highly, as having been in battle against a king.” We’re reading what happened for our forefathers aforetime. If the Most High didn’t forsake our forefathers then, he’s not going to forsake us now. And we got to believe that.

sense.text:
“Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith”. Draw near to God with a true heart and full assurance of faith. Don’t half step it: either you believe it or you don’t. With a true heart, not with dissimulation.

“Having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience”: the evilness we’re putting behind us and pressing toward the righteousness. Stay to your own mind long enough, stop being around when there’s opportunity to fellowship, and your evil conscience is going to take over, and you’re going to be destroyed even though you see the day approaching. That’s the scariest thing: knowing the end, seeing all of the prophecies come to pass, but you cannot get over the hump because you didn’t let go of that evil conscience.

“And our bodies washed with pure water.”

“Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering”. You wouldn’t even consider wavering if everything was just cool. It’s saying without wavering, understanding the opposition, the adversity, the perils that we’re going to be going through and are going through right now. “For he is faithful that promised.”

“And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works”. Like in 2 Maccabees, we got to keep each other in prayer, consider one another, provoke each other to good works, so we can build our faith and our belief to stand in the times of trouble.

“Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together”. We’ve been through hell in our various captivities: slavery, Jim Crow in the South, sundown towns, all the evil decrees and legislation constantly passed against us and things being developed in the dark. The Most High is saying, even in your captivity, even amongst the other nations that hate you and despise you, I still allowed you to have these little sanctuaries. How dare you not go to them? How dare you not be amongst the brethren and the sisters to get your spirit recharged?

“As the manner of some is”. That’s why he spared a grape of the cluster, not all of them, because everybody ain’t right. Everybody is not going to dig and try to rise above it. Someone may be wronging you in this truth, but how do you know if you’re approved, if you’re chosen? By what you do after that. You could strive with words, go to fisticuffs, devise evil, or you can love your enemy as Christ commanded. It’s a choice. A lot of people, when things like that take place, chuck the deuces and start separating themselves, like it says in the book of Jude: they who separate themselves don’t have the spirit. Every last one of us is going to have that make-or-break moment, and if you don’t fully believe with all assurance, it’s going to show as the persecution increases.

“But exhorting one another”: even the brother or sister that wronged you. You got to continue to be righteous. This is our reasonable service, what we owe to God. You can’t love God if you can’t love your brother or sister that’s right in front of you.

“And so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.” That’s the key. There’s more heartache and betrayal coming, things that are going to get on your nerves, but brother and sister, y’all better tuck it in, because we see the day approaching. You don’t know if you can forgive him for that? Is he still in the faith? Is she still in the faith? Then you better forgive, because the end is near; the day of the Lord is approaching. If we feel that, go harder, and try to be around even more to combat that evil spirit.

precepts.why:
“Thus saith the Lord God; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.” A little sanctuary. All praise to the Most High: he set this thing up for us to get strength.

These little sanctuaries are like a charging station. You come in on the Sabbath and the feast days and you get recharged, your spirit gets lifted back up, so we can fight the evils out there. So how dare you not go to them? That is the assembling of ourselves together that we must not forsake.

sense.text:
This portion is: we will need to be at our absolute best to endure the trials to come.

“For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Israel is the Lord’s portion”. Of all the people on the face of the earth, he chose us. We belong to him.
“Whom, being his firstborn, he nourisheth with discipline, and giving him the light of his love doth not forsake him.” The Most High is not forsaking his people, contrary to what the nations say.

“Therefore all their works are as the sun before him”. He chose us and he’s not going to forsake us, but therefore all their works, the good and the evil, are before him, so we really got to make sure and be mindful. “And his eyes are continually upon their ways.”

“None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from him”. Not one. You may have forgot about it, but the Lord did not. Who in this room was born in the truth? Your evil right now outweighs your good, so it would be in our best interest to increase in the righteousness. There’s no mountain of righteousness where you say, okay, that’s a good limit. Why sit back when you could put your hand to the plow every day?

“But the Lord being gracious and knowing his workmanship, neither left nor forsook them, but spared them.” You think he’s going to spare the wicked? Absolutely not. He’s talking about a specific group within that nation: the righteous, that grape of the cluster.

precepts.why:
“All their works”: that’s the good and the evil. “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing”. He’s looking at us, because the whole thing is about us. Like The Truman Show: that’s a similitude of the nation of Israel. All eyes were on Jim Carrey; he was the star; he played Truman. We’re the star of this world. Everything we do, the spotlight’s on it, the good acts and the bad acts.

So we always got to have that mindset: right now ain’t no time for slipping. If I slip, I got to get back up, because that’s going to show character. If I want to hide everything and not have a true heart, all of those things are being documented and recorded, and eventually I’m going to have to give an account for all of those works.

Why sit back? We have to tap into our true potential. We’re supposed to be righteous beings on this earth, and because the world is so wicked, we have to rise up. “I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. So we have to consider that.

To stay in the same mindset as what we just read in chapter 17. “For the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee, and to give up thine enemies before thee”. The ultimate goal of the Most High is to spare his people, and he can see every work. We have an angel assigned to all of us. He walks in the midst of our camp, and for all those that don’t believe in camps, there it is in the Bible.

“Therefore shall thy camp be holy: that he see no unclean thing in thee, and turn away from thee.” The Lord’s not going to fight for us, not going to deliver us, if we are not in the spirit, if we’re in the midst of sin.

We cannot fight against the unknown out there. Like it said in Maccabees, only God knows what they’re coming up with to fight against us. It has to be God on our side. “The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.” If we’re in the spirit, if we’re doing what’s right, God said he’ll fight for us.

sense.text: God created us for his purpose and for his glory. Our job is to understand just that: not to try to figure it out on our own, but to figure out exactly what God wants us to do. So he prays “that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him.”

“The eyes of your understanding being enlightened.” Keep this in mind. Do not take the gift you have for granted. The Most High did not enlighten everybody to the knowledge of being an Israelite, that the world was created for you, that God is black and Christ is black. God pulled you out of the matrix. We were living in the same world before, but now we see clearly. We see things differently because the Most High saw fit to open our eyes, so we could see the truth and what is really going on in the world.

“That ye may know what is the hope of his calling.” If you don’t have discernment, if you feel lost, if you don’t have a clue, you need to pray and fast and be amongst the righteous, so you can start developing and learning what you are called for. Some brothers and sisters don’t know, and that is not good. If you don’t know why you keep going to the Sabbath, why you wear fringes and don’t eat pork, that is an issue. You better repent, fast and pray so you can get on board with the Most High’s program.

“And what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.” Know why we do what we do: so we can inherit an incorruptible crown and live forever, because the earth was created for us.

Don’t allow one isolated incident in your walk to dictate the rest of your being. If you understand the hope of your calling, there are certain things you won’t do. Even when you see the evil, you remember: God didn’t call me for this, he called me to do what he told me to do. Never forget that. There is never an excuse to support the evil. Somebody is going to try to pull you out of the spirit, but that is the test, the condition of the battle: I can’t let them, I have to stay focused and stay in the spirit, because I know the hope of my calling and I am trying to achieve that incorruptible crown.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more”. That is how we know for sure this is us. We have been through it all: Section 8, police brutality, whatever it may be. That is the bread of adversity and the water of affliction.

“But thine eyes shall see thy teachers.” You may have run into your calling on the street corners of New York or Atlanta, or you may have been surfing YouTube and run into your teacher there. Understand that it was the Most High that called you and enlightened you, so you could understand the hope of your calling. You have to see it like that.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.” Walk ye in it. We didn’t know the way. We were lost; we had no clue. But the Most High saw fit to put the spirit on that prophet to enlighten you and call you out of this wicked world.

You have been given that gift. The Most High chose you. Now it is up to you to fulfill your purpose. That is what tapping into your full potential is.

“For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus”: we are his creation. “Unto good works”: that is what we are supposed to do. Once we hear ‘This is the way, walk ye in it’, now we have to perform those good works. Don’t sit around. Don’t waste time. Put your hand to the plow and do the work.

“Which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.” Walk in them. As soon as you were called, that is when you realized this is why God made you in the first place. As soon as you heard: God is black, Christ is black, you have to keep the commandments, you can’t shave your beard no more, you have to wear fringes, this is the way, walk ye in it. Then you realize, that’s why God created me.

God ordained this before you were even sent here. So why kick against the pricks? Why delay and put yourself in jeopardy of missing out on the reward, living forever in the kingdom of heaven?

precepts.why: The class reads on in the same chapter and jumps down to verse 13: “But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” We are created in Christ Jesus unto good works, and in Christ Jesus we who were far off are made nigh.

sense.text:
“I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called.” We have to make sure we walk upright, that we walk worthy, so that God doesn’t say, ‘Damn, I repent for even calling this brother or sister.’ You don’t want that said about you. As soon as you are called and shown the way, it is best that you walk worthy of your calling, because he didn’t call everybody. We can’t take this walk or this truth for granted.

God called us to be the leaders, the saviors in these last days, to show the right example to our people. God has expectations for every last one of us, and we have to live up to them. It is our job to put the emotions to the side and stay on course, no matter what comes against us. That is not why you were sent here. You were sent here to do the job. So do it.

precepts.why:
One of the famous ones the ex-Christians know: “I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.” That is fact. Some of you may have doubts; it is time to put the doubts away. That is not biblical. He said to walk worthy of the vocation.

Sometimes to walk worthy you have to put certain people on the back burner, separate yourself from certain people. If they are not exhorting you and helping you get to where God has called you to be, the longer you are with them, the more you are just prolonging it and putting your soul in jeopardy. Whatever outside factor goes against your calling, it is up to you to make those decisions, because we are commanded to walk worthy according to our calling. If you feel that dead weight, it is time to separate from it, whatever it is: addictions, lust, an innumerable amount of things.

You know best. Don’t be the brother who comes up for counsel and says, ‘What do I need to do? What do you see in me?’ Negro, you know what the hell you do. You know what the hell you are going through. It is up to you to put that to the side and overcome that thing, through Christ which strengtheneth you.

sense.text:
You can’t walk worthy and overcome if you have fear. It isn’t possible. You are not going to be able to continue and overcome with the spirit of fear.

“Be strong and of a good courage.” You have to be strong. “Fear not, nor be afraid of them”: even though they are coming up with things in the dark against you, whatever it is or whoever it is, God said be strong and of a good courage.

“For the Lord thy God, he it is that doth go with thee.” You have to believe that, and you cannot forget it. “He will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.” He will not fail you, nor forsake you. Understand that thing.

precepts.why:
If it happens, that means God allowed it. If you are put in that situation, God allowed it, so you have to go with it. You have to stop doubting and trust God.

“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” Don’t fear those who have the power to kill the body. That is what it is all about. Keep your trust in the Lord, the true power, the only power. That is why we can fear not, nor be afraid of them.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” It is God that put that in us. He gave us a sound mind, because he has our back. He is the one who goes with us, just as Deuteronomy says: “he it is that doth go with thee.”

sense.text:
Why do you keep allowing fear to stop you, to get in your way? Death is appointed to every man, so you only have so much time while you are on the earth. Why would you allow fear to stop you or get in your way from being great? The prophet says the same exact thing: “Who shall praise the most High in the grave, instead of them which live and give thanks?” Nobody. Nobody praises him in the grave. Now is your time to be great. Some people ask, is now a good time? Yes, now is the time. Now is not the time to be scared.

At the end of the day, Israel wins. Israel is going to be the winner. So why are we scared? When you go into a burning building, you only think about getting what you have to get and getting out, and we have to be like that too. That is what we read in Matthew 10:28: who cares about those who can kill your body? You have to fear God, because he has the keys to the kingdom. That is the mindset to have. We shouldn’t be fearful of these other things. You may feel it, but don’t act on that feeling. That is the key.

Judas Maccabeus “and they that were with him, went privily into the towns”, gathered all “such as continued in the Jews’ religion, and assembled about six thousand men.” “And they called upon the Lord, that he would look upon the people that was trodden down of all; and also pity the temple profaned of ungodly men.” They called upon the Lord.

“So when Philip saw that this man increased by little and little”: this man is Judas Maccabeus. “And that things prospered with him still more and more”, so Philip wrote to the governor “to yield more aid to the king’s affairs.”

He chose Nicanor “the son of Patroclus, one of his special friends”, and “sent him with no fewer than twenty thousand of all nations under him.” They called on Nicanor to come against our forefather Judas Maccabeus, because he was doing much work and putting many to death. He was a problem they couldn’t deal with.

They are still dealing with fear here. “When word was brought unto Judas of Nicanor’s coming, and he had imparted unto those that were with him that the army was at hand”: he told his men, Nicanor is coming against us; the army is at hand.

“They that were fearful, and distrusted the justice of God, fled, and conveyed themselves away.” They distrusted the justice of God. When the trouble comes on this side, brothers and sisters, those who are fearful are going to do the exact same thing. And that is going to be your name, something you can’t undo. Build yourselves up. Tap into your full potential so this doesn’t end up being you.

“Others sold all that they had left, and withal besought the Lord to deliver them.” The others had full assurance and full confidence; they trusted that the Lord would deliver them, though they were “sold by the wicked Nicanor before they met together.” So you have a choice: flee with the fearful, or trust the Lord to deliver you.
Still dealing with fear. “And, lo, I perceived that God had not sent him; but that he pronounced this prophecy against me: for Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.”

“Therefore was he hired, that I should be afraid.” That is the job of the nations: to put fear in us and to stop the building. So we can’t fall into the trap.

“That I should be afraid, and do so, and sin.” To be fearful is sin. “And that they might have matter for an evil report, that they might reproach me.” The fear they put in us is meant to give them a reproach against us.

The longer we doubt, the longer we have fear, the longer we are not pleasing in the sight of God: “But without faith it is impossible to please him.” So we have to let go of that. We have to let go of the weak nature, and the weak nature is going into addictions and distractions, things like social media, lust, whatever it may be. We have to let go of these things.

“Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh.” Remember what we read earlier in Ecclesiasticus 17: the Most High watches all of our works, good and bad. So we have to make sure we cleanse ourselves, so we can tap into our full potential.

We have to cleanse ourselves and abstain from that. You have to abstain.

We have to cleanse ourselves from all uncleanness, and we have to abstain so we can overcome. Now’s the time to do it; now’s the time to tap into that full potential.

“Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” But you can’t be like the fearful of our people when the army was coming against us, doubting the Lord. You can’t do that. You have to put your full assurance and your trust in the Lord in order to resist.

Going into abstaining. “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”. That is going to put the fear in you. Think about it: when you’re in the spirit, when you have a pattern of good works, you feel confident. You know you’re doing what’s right; God got me. But as soon as that sin enters in, what comes in? Doubt. Fear. It’s like, damn, I think I lost my covering, man; I don’t know if the Most High got me.

So the best thing to do, brothers and sisters, is to build our spirits up to abstain, so we know without a shadow of a doubt that the Lord’s going to fight for us. “Abstain from fleshly lusts”.
“Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” He careth for you if you care for him. That’s the key. It’s not a one-sided relationship. Don’t forget that, brothers and sisters.

precepts.why:
He cares for you if you care for him. “I love them that love me”: you see that? It’s a relationship, a give and take.

“And those that seek me early shall find me.” Remember when it was asked earlier, when’s the time? Now’s the time. Right now is early. Early simply means before the destruction comes. That’s it; that’s all it means.

sense.text: Read to elaborate on seeking him early. “O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.” This is going into the kingdom: “let us walk in the light of the Lord.” Now it’s about to switch.

“Therefore thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines”. These are those of us who didn’t have that full assurance in Christ, who were walking like the other nations in our sins. “And they please themselves in the children of strangers.”

“Their land also is full of silver and gold”: this is the covetous that are amongst us, the materialistic. “Neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots”.

“Their land also is full of idols”. The book of Ezekiel chapter 14 goes into the idols and the idolatry our people are involved in. And understand this: porn is an idol. A cigarette is an idol. Drunkenness is an idol. “They worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made”.

Don’t forget the point, why we came here: the Lord said he loves those who love him, and those who seek him early shall find him. Meaning before it gets bad, before the destruction comes.

“And the mean man boweth down”: that man that’s on high, who’s full of all those possessions, he’s going to bow down. Why would he try to bow down? Because he sees what’s popping off, and he doesn’t want to be forgotten.

There is a timetable with God. Understand that thing right there. God don’t deal with everybody the same. Some of us can reject this truth one time and then he’ll give you over, like it says in 2 Thessalonians 2: he’ll give you to believe that lie. So don’t take this for granted; there is a time limit with the Most High God.

“And the great man humbleth himself: therefore forgive them not.” Forgive them not, because they didn’t seek him early. They didn’t seek him when they had the time. They said, I’m going to do what I want to do, and now: expiration. The time has run out. Don’t let that be you, because you have the gift. You have this knowledge now. Don’t cast this behind your back.

“Be sober, be vigilant”. If you’re always caught up in your addiction, how can you be sober-minded? If you’re in the midst of sin, you can’t think clear; you can’t trust your thoughts in the midst of sin. “Be vigilant”: you can’t have foresight, you can’t have discernment. The spirit ain’t rolling with you when you’re in the midst of sin.

“Because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. And now your protection’s gone. You don’t have the spiritual discernment, you don’t have your guard up, and when it’s crunch time you can’t defend yourself against the devil. So, brothers and sisters, let’s make sure that we are girding ourselves up.

We got to get rid of these addictions, these hang-ups that plague us on the daily. “And this I speak for your own profit; not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is comely, and that ye may attend upon the Lord without distraction.” We have to learn how to eliminate these distractions, brothers and sisters.

“They received the use of the five operations of the Lord”: God’s creation, mankind, received the five uses, the five senses: see, taste, smell, hear, and feel or touch. Those are the five.

“And in the sixth place he imparted them understanding.” Does everybody have understanding? No. Everybody does not have understanding. What follows are examples of what happens when you don’t roll in understanding, and how we need to pray for the understanding.

precepts.why: “The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again.” So the topic of discussion is God creating man, mankind, and verse 5 is what he did for his creation.

An example of the forefather. “Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him” his son: King Solomon passed away and his son Rehoboam took over. There isn’t time today to go over that history, but go read up on it in 1 Kings 11 and 1 Kings 12.

“Even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding”. He had the five senses, but he lacked understanding, and those who study the history know what happened because of his actions. “Who turned away the people through his counsel”: his counsel wasn’t godly. It was carnal, without understanding. “There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin”.

Knowing how detrimental things can become if you don’t have understanding, brothers and sisters, we got to go to the Father and pray for that thing.
Praying for understanding. “Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.”

God gave us teachers and leaders and fathers and mothers on the earth to help us. It’s like Marvel and DC: they get these powers, but they don’t know how to fully harness them, so they had to be tutored, like the X-Men, with Xavier training and schooling them so they can hone in and use their powers to the full potential. Same thing: now that God called you and showed you that this is the way, you got to walk in it, and he also gave you some tutors to help you harness it, control it and use it the right way.

“Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities.” It’s not going to kill you; it’s not going to break your head. So take that correction. You’re learning, you’re going to make your mistakes, so don’t bug out; keep going.

That correction is going to allow you to be the best version of you, ultimately to tap into your full potential, and to teach you understanding. You don’t have that until God calls you and touches you, and your leaders mold you so you can tap into it at the higher level.

To go along with that: “So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.” They gave the sense; that sense is the understanding. That’s the sixth part right there.

sense.text:
“For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.” Contextually this is talking about the ex-Pharisees, those leaders that were set up: you may think you have an understanding, but now you got to be taught again; you got to be taught Christ. And we can use it this way: you may be called, you may think you know something, but now you got to be taught all over again.

The importance of that milk: in the carnal sense, milk has literally everything a newborn needs to survive on, and that’s why the Most High uses that example. As long as you’re keeping God’s commandments, you’ll be spared in that time. The key is to tap into your full potential and stay there, and never think you’ve outgrown the basics. The laws are the basic understanding to keep us properly nourished. Even when you get to the meat, the harder things, you still have to keep that going and keep exercising your senses so you can stay at that level.
“For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.”

“But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised”. That’s the key. In order to tap into your full potential, you have to have your senses exercised. You got to go through trials, you got to go through tribulations, so you can learn the proper understanding and know how to give the counsel: what should I do in this situation. You got to go through it. You can’t just wake up and be a captain or a deacon or a bishop. It takes time to get there.

precepts.why: “As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby”. It has to be a constant desire. You can’t let your fire or your lamp burn out. It has to be constant, because you may jump up here, but you’ll start to decline if you don’t properly nourish yourself.

We were all born with the five senses, but the sixth one, you have to be chosen for that thing.

“But they also have erred through wine”: that wine is the lies. We’ve all erred at one point; all of us have been guilty of sin at one point. “And through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment.” Just like the forefather Jeroboam: when it came to his counsel he stumbled, and it caused a whole nation to suffer from it. When you go outside of God’s design you choose the wrong beverage. That’s heavy right there: you chose the strong drink and not the milk.

“For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.” Now we’re going into the healing: like we read earlier in 2 Corinthians 7, we have to cleanse ourselves from all uncleanness.

“Whom shall he teach knowledge?” Who’s he going to teach this wisdom and knowledge to? “And whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” That’s the sixth sense: who’s he going to make to understand his doctrine? “Them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.” You can’t tap into your full potential until you master the milk. There’s no other way to do it. And in these times, now’s not the time to be playing. Now is the time to be in the milk constantly, to study. Otherwise you’re going to leave yourself out there high and dry, putting yourself in the danger zone for the adversary to catch you by yourself.

sense.text: “When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.” We have to continue to grow. And when we tap into that understanding, we have to have the mindset that we’re not going to let anything or anyone jeopardize us from losing that potential. It’s not about feelings or emotions; it’s not about pleasures or self-satisfaction. Make sure once you tap in, you don’t let that thing go.

precepts.why: “Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.” The quit right there means to convey or behave. So it says behave like men, and be strong, with courage, without fear.

“Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind”: of your mind. It’s not carnal. In this world we think being a man is the brother that can turn up, go from zero to 100 and put hands on you. God is telling us to be strong men according to the Bible, and a strong man is all about his mind, his spirit. He can control his spirit, no matter where people are trying to sway you, whether to the left or to the right.

“Be sober”: let go of the addiction. Let go of the other doctrines. It’s time to be men; it’s not time to be a child tossed to and fro anymore. “And hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ”: keep the hope, keep the faith, don’t have fear. That revelation is in Zechariah 12, when we see the revealing of Christ, when we see him return. So keep the faith and don’t waver to the end.

sense.text:
Things that can keep us in the spirit, that can keep us at that level once we reach our full potential: fasting humbles your spirit. “But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting”. We have to humble our soul with fasting. When you fast, it’s a spiritual booster. Like the video showed, you may be trying to fight the porn, the social media, the gluttony, whatever it may be; in a carnal sense your flesh is very weak, but when you fast you’re tapping into your spirit. You may hit your potential, but when you fast it’s going to be enhanced, at another level, and it’s going to give you more strength to fight. So all of you that are medically capable are encouraged to increase in fasting.

“And my prayer returned into mine own bosom.”

precepts.why:
The leadership has been encouraging us to pray as our forefathers did, constantly, three times a day, to pray without ceasing. “Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice.”

So if we want the Lord to fight for us, what do we got to do? First and foremost, not be in the midst of sin; that’s number one, because if God is in the midst of us, he sees it all. Number two, we got to tap into our full potential: study, pray, apply, everything we went over today. Next, fasting and praying. It’s going to enhance your spirit, so the Lord can hear you clearer.

sense.text: “That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work”: like we read earlier, that’s why he created us. “And increasing in the knowledge of God.” Because if you’re not increasing, by default you’re getting worse. So once you tap into that full potential, you have to sustain the full potential, and grow upon it and build upon it.

“Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son”. We were doomed. We were caught up in our lust, our idols, whatever it may be, but God saw fit to enlighten us, to open up our eyes.
“Even the forgiveness of sins.” Now is the time, brothers and sisters.

In closing: it’s time for us to ramp up and tap into this full potential. Of course we’re going to watch and pray; we have to know what’s going on, but don’t let that put fear in you, family.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God”. Like it says in Matthew 24:14, us going through these afflictions is making a witness to the power of God, because Christ already told us this would happen. So by us going through this boldly, with fortitude, trusting and believing and carrying his will out, that’s a witness against the nations.

“Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling”: a holy calling. “Not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began”. We have to figure out God’s purpose, and ultimately we have to be worthy of the calling.
